standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic workplace boundaries task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: Three scenario cards describe a fictional grocery bagger asked to run a register alone without training, a fictional lawn-crew member asked by a coworker to cover a shift without telling the supervisor, and a fictional library shelver asked by a patron for their personal phone number.
safetyNotes: Maple Ridge Market, GreenPath Lawn Crew, and Elm Street Public Library are fictional; no scenario describes or requires a real employer or real supervisor.

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g8-u05-l05-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g8-u05-l05-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g8-u05-l05-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g8-u05-l05-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Which of the three scenarios was hardest to decide, and what specifically made choosing a response harder there than in the other two?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g8-u05-l05-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g8-u05-l05-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g8-u05-l05-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Boundary identification: The response choice correctly addresses the specific boundary at stake in all three scenarios. | Justification quality: Each justification names the specific boundary at risk and explains why the chosen response protects it. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g8-u05-l05-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner write a fourth original workplace-boundary scenario of their own, set at a different fictional business, along with two response options and an explanation of which one is better and why.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic workplace boundaries task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

localMaterials.label: paper or a document
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

materials.noPurchaseRule: No purchase is required. Use the complete fictional route when a local material, setting, source, or adult is unavailable.

resources.title: workplace boundaries worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: Three scenario cards describe a fictional grocery bagger asked to run a register alone without training, a fictional lawn-crew member asked by a coworker to cover a shift without telling the supervisor, and a fictional library shelver asked by a patron for their personal phone number.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact workplace boundaries decision or action.
Model move 2: Before reading the scenario cards, think about what the phrase 'workplace boundary' means.
Model move 3: Read the grocery-register scenario card: a fictional bagger at Maple Ridge Market is asked to run the register alone even though they have never been trained on it.

Model check: Boundary identification: The response choice correctly addresses the specific boundary at stake in all three scenarios. | Justification quality: Each justification names the specific boundary at risk and explains why the chosen response protects it.

resources.title: workplace boundaries action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for workplace boundaries.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: workplace boundaries coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: Three scenario cards describe a fictional grocery bagger asked to run a register alone without training, a fictional lawn-crew member asked by a coworker to cover a shift without telling the supervisor, and a fictional library shelver asked by a patron for their personal phone number.
Coach direction: Before reading the scenario cards, think about what the phrase 'workplace boundary' means.
Learner prompt: In your own words, explain what a workplace boundary is, and give one example of a boundary a first-time worker might have.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: workplace boundaries complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Read the grocery-register scenario card: a fictional bagger at Maple Ridge Market is asked to run the register alone even though they have never been trained on it. Choose the best response and explain your reasoning.
Response 1 (t2-p1): What should the fictional bagger do first?
Response 2 (t2-p2): Explain why the option you chose respects both the bagger's actual training and the store's need to have the register covered safely.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: workplace boundaries minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Which of the three scenarios was hardest to decide, and what specifically made choosing a response harder there than in the other two?

Success checks: Boundary identification: The response choice correctly addresses the specific boundary at stake in all three scenarios. | Justification quality: Each justification names the specific boundary at risk and explains why the chosen response protects it.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: workplace boundaries supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g8-u05-l05-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g8-u05-l05-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional workplace boundaries condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Boundary identification: The response choice correctly addresses the specific boundary at stake in all three scenarios. | Justification quality: Each justification names the specific boundary at risk and explains why the chosen response protects it..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g8-u05-l05-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

simulationRoute.title: workplace boundaries — complete fictional route
simulationRoute.directions: Complete the workplace boundaries task using the fictional condition and invented, non-sensitive details on the delivered independent card.
simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

independentTask.privacyAlternative: The learner may use invented names, dates, amounts, organizations, spaces, and circumstances whenever real details are unnecessary or private.

learnerEvidence: one revision when a step changed
evidence.reflectionPrompt: Which of the three scenarios was hardest to decide, and what specifically made choosing a response harder there than in the other two?
observableCriteria: Boundary identification: The response choice correctly addresses the specific boundary at stake in all three scenarios.
Justification quality: Each justification names the specific boundary at risk and explains why the chosen response protects it.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g8-u05-l05-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g8-u05-l05-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g8-u05-l05-retry-pair without the coach prompt.
retry.exitCriterion: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Boundary identification: The response choice correctly addresses the specific boundary at stake in all three scenarios. | Justification quality: Each justification names the specific boundary at risk and explains why the chosen response protects it.
retry.returnPath: Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g8-u05-l05-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
